input: SC-LU-VEGETA-001 — Lineup decode: Vegeta, the Sovereignty pole (Ultra Ego). Handed to Frieza as a child and kept in his service, who keeps the will to exist as his own entity; survives the Spirit Bomb; fuses with Goku (Vegito, Gogeta). Shax (t570u): Vegeta is Lucifer; Satan is Frieza and the Frieza race.

metadata.title: Lineup Decode: Vegeta — The Sovereignty Pole (Ultra Ego)

addenda.note: Shax ruling t568u (2026-11-25), RUL-BINARY-001: SC-DU-001 (The Duality) and SC-MD-001 (Sovereign Mirror Duality) are the same invariant: a binary whose only stable outcomes are mutual cooperation or mutual destruction. Instances: Oneness/Sovereignty (SC-CP-001), God/Satan (theological mapping), and our universe / the CPT-mirrored universe (SC-LU-FRIEZA-001 layer D). Hub: SC-MIRROR-001 CLM-MIRROR-006. Graded ISOMORPHIC_INVARIANT (structural equivalence claim by Shax); no physics or theology claim is upgraded and no score changes.

addenda.quote: I suppose you could say their was only Mutual Co operation.... Or Hang yourself and Lose anyway.
addenda.note: RUL-BINARY-001 rev 2 (Shax t571u, 2026-11-25): the only stable outcome of the binary is mutual cooperation. Refusal is self-destruction: the refusing side destroys itself and loses regardless. Its information-conserving remnant is compressed into SC-MIRROR-001's calibration dot (the white-field / black-dot target state) and Oneness prevails. Rev 1's 'mutual destruction' is reframed as the refuser's self-destruction, not a symmetric stable outcome. This resolves SC-VESSEL-001's open question in favour of reading B (refinement, not a third outcome). Grade unchanged (ISOMORPHIC_INVARIANT, structural claim by Shax); no score changed. Fitting examples: Sukuna (JJK ch. 268: refuses, disintegrates; Yuji keeps Shrine and soul perception) and Kid Buu (Spirit Bomb; reincarnated as Uub, partial fit). Vegeta's consented fusion (Vegito, Gogeta) is the cooperation outcome; Majin Vegeta's Final Explosion is a sacrifice, not a refusal, so it is not a rev 2 example.

addenda.quote: Vegeta is sovreignty, Lucifer. Freeza the Outsider Enslaving Lucifer In Hell, But its not like Lucifer didn't enjoy what they were doing...
addenda.note: Shax (t572u, 2026-11-25 19:30 America/Halifax): 'Vegeta is sovreignty, Lucifer. Freeza the Outsider Enslaving Lucifer In Hell, But its not like Lucifer didn't enjoy what they were doing...' Dated Shax interpretation, recorded as CLM-LU-VEG-09: complicit enslavement. The Sovereignty pole is owned by the outsider (Frieza/Satan) yet willingly enjoys the work, so the bondage is partly self-chosen. Canon, tradition and interpretation are separate layers. Canon support: DB ch. 213 (planet-trade / 'let's go play'); ch. 249 (smiling execution of Cui, after he has already broken from Frieza); ch. 308 (admission of service and obedience, not enjoyment); ch. 456–457 (lets Babidi's spell in to recover the ruthless self; motive is rivalry with Goku); DBS manga ch. 69 (admits Saiyan/Frieza-era invasions as sins and will not lay all blame on Frieza; later guilt recorded). Anime-original: DBZ 'Trouble on Arlia' (Japanese ep. 11). Tradition/literature, not scripture: Milton, Paradise Lost I.263 ('Better to reign in Hell, than serve in Heav'n'). Linked to RUL-BINARY-001 rev 2 as the refusal state during the ownership period; Vegeta later takes the cooperation branch (fusion). SILVER 0.85 unchanged; no grade or score changed.

Merged as rev 1.2.0, not a duplicate ID. Source claims CLM-VEGETA-001..005 become CLM-LU-VEG-10..14 (source_claim_id kept). Self-grade GOLD 0.92 not accepted. scale_integrity 0.75 -> 0.8 (cosmological mapping added); corpus_completeness 0.85 -> 0.9 (Goku counterpart compiled). Composite 0.85 -> 0.862; tier SILVER unchanged (GOLD needs every gate >= 0.8; measurement_integrity is 0.7). CLM-LU-VEG-13 scope-limited to internal drives under RUL-BINARY-001 rev 2.

claims.label: SOVEREIGNTY POLE — ULTRA EGO
claims.text: Vegeta is the Sovereignty pole of the Oneness/Sovereignty binary. Canon anchor: Ultra Ego (DBS manga ch. 74, 'Vegeta Vs. Granolah'), learned from Beerus, gives a God of Destruction's ki and grows with damage taken and fighting spirit. Its Japanese name, Wagamama no Goku'i, reads 'the secret of the self-indulgent': self-assertion, the opposite of Ultra Instinct's letting go (Goku, Oneness).

evidence.text: Vegeta unlocks Ultra Ego against Granolah; he lets himself take hits to grow stronger and ends the fight spent.

evidence.source: creator commentary as reported by fan wiki (dragon-ballwiki.com, 'Ultra Ego')
evidence.text: Toyotarou designed Ultra Ego and Ultra Instinct as yin and yang; Vegeta calls Ultra Ego the polar opposite of Ultra Instinct.

residuals: The pole assignment is the compiler's mapping (SC-CP-001, SC-OMNI-001); canon fixes the form, not the theology.
Ultra Ego's growth-through-damage leaves Vegeta spent by the end of ch. 75: the pole may carry its own failure mode.

claims.label: PRINCE GIVEN AS AN OFFERING
claims.text: Shax (t570u): Vegeta was 'forced to Work for the Man by Fate. Design. By his Father. As an offering.' Canon support depends on the version.

versions.text: King Vegeta had agreed to hand Prince Vegeta to Frieza and regretted it; Frieza reminds him of the promise; King Vegeta leads a mutiny to get his son back and is killed; Frieza destroys Planet Vegeta.

versions.source: Dragon Ball manga (Saiyan and Namek arcs)
versions.text: The Saiyans worked for Frieza and Vegeta served in his army. The manga does not show the handover scene.

versions.source: Dragon Ball Minus (2014); Dragon Ball Super: Broly (2018)
versions.text: The Saiyans serve the Cold Force, which King Cold hands to Frieza. King Vegeta resents it ('That monster Frieza thinks the Saiyans will serve him without question. But he'll fall to us'). The films do not show him surrendering his son.

residuals: 'By his Father, as an offering' matches the DBZ anime version only; in Minus/Broly the service is subjugation the father resents, not a handover he makes.
Anime-original material is counted under Shax's evidence ruling and labelled so it can be filtered.

claims.label: SERVES THE OPPRESSOR, KEEPS HIS OWN WILL
claims.text: Vegeta serves in Frieza's army while keeping the will to exist as his own entity: he calls himself the Prince of all Saiyans throughout, plans to kill Frieza, and on Namek refuses Frieza's offer to return, saying he obeyed only to wait for his chance (DBZ; manga Namek arc). In DBS ch. 74 he tells Granolah he is no longer part of Frieza's army. Sovereignty under ownership: compliance without surrender of identity.

claims.label: SPIRIT BOMB STRUCTURAL RESPONSE
claims.text: Krillin throws the Spirit Bomb, Vegeta dodges, Gohan bounces it back, and it hits Vegeta directly; he survives, badly hurt (DB ch. 238). Goku's stated rule is that a pure heart can deflect it. Vegeta, who is not pure-hearted, survives anyway, so the outcome is not a moral verdict. Evidence for SC-SB-001's COLLECTIVE INPUT / STRUCTURAL RESPONSE child invariant alongside Frieza (survives) and Kid Buu (destroyed).
residuals: magnitude confound: the Saiyan-arc Spirit Bomb drew on part of Earth only
with films and GT counted, kills are Dr. Wheelo, Turles, Lord Slug, Kid Buu and Omega Shenron; survivors are Vegeta, Frieza and Jiren

claims.label: FUSION — THE COOPERATION BRANCH
claims.text: Fusion of the Sovereignty pole with the Oneness pole is the cooperation outcome of RUL-BINARY-001 and SC-MIRROR-001's anti-deadlock claim: Vegito (Potara, Buu arc manga) and Gogeta (Fusion Dance: Fusion Reborn 1995, Dragon Ball Super: Broly 2018; Super Saiyan 4 Gogeta against Omega Shenron in GT). Both personalities persist in the fused warrior and the output exceeds either alone.
claims.consent: Vegeta refuses fusion out of pride and agrees only after his own evaluation (Vegito: after learning Bulma had been killed by Buu). Cooperation is reached by consent, not coercion: the 'both agree' branch of the SC-VESSEL-001 resolution rule.
residuals: Fusion is time-limited (Fusion Dance, 30 minutes) or broken from inside (Vegito defuses inside Buu); the cooperation state is temporary in canon.
The Potara earrings were permanent for mortals in the Buu arc but later shown to wear off for non-gods (DBS); version detail, not load-bearing here.

claims.label: MAJIN VEGETA AND THE FINAL EXPLOSION — VSR CHECK
claims.text: Canon: Vegeta lets Babidi's spell in to recover his old ruthless self and fight Goku (ch. 456); Babidi admits he is not under full control. After Buu emerges, Vegeta knocks Goku out to face Buu alone, hugs Trunks for the first time, and self-destructs with the Final Explosion (ch. 467). Piccolo: he fought for someone other than himself for the first time. Buu regenerates.

invariants.information_preservation: PARTIAL (dies; later revived and returns with his body)
invariants.latent_reversibility: FAIL as recompression: the act spends his life, it does not settle into a lower stable capability

vsr_check.reading: Majin acceptance is the inverse of VSR: a voluntary removal of restraint to regain power (closer to SC-LU-FRIEZA-001's restraint removal). The Final Explosion is self-sacrifice, not recompression.

claims.repo_reading: V7 §15.1 (Curtis Theological Map) reads the Majin arc as Lucifer's redemption: accepting corruption to compete, redeemed by self-sacrifice for love. Recorded as Shax's prior interpretation (ANALOGOUS).

claims.label: LUCIFER MAPPING (SHAX INTERPRETATION)
claims.text: Shax (t570u): 'Vegeta is Lucifer. Satan is Frieza, the Frieza race.' Lucifer and Satan are distinct: Lucifer is the Sovereignty pole, 'the will to exist as their own entity', held in the external owner's service; Satan is the owner. The same split is in V7 §15.1 ('Frieza enslaved Vegeta' / 'Satan (separate entity) enslaved Lucifer'). No theological claim is upgraded.
tensions: Tradition identifies Lucifer with Satan. The split diverges from tradition but fits the bare text: Isa 14:12 ('morning star') never names Satan, and Rev 12:9 names the dragon Satan without naming Lucifer.
Internal repo tension: V7 §22.4 uses Vegeta's arc as Satan's trajectory, and V7 §22.5 places Lucifer as the Holy Spirit; t569u places the vessel as the Holy Spirit. Recorded, not resolved.
claims.effect_on_ruling: RUL-BINARY-001's God/Satan instance reads God (Oneness) ↔ Lucifer/Vegeta (Sovereignty), with Satan/Frieza outside the binary as the owner. Revelation's defeat of the dragon (Rev 12:7–9) then concerns the owner, not the opposite pole.

claims.label: SCALE MAPPINGS
claims.text: AI: a model's own capability and objectives held inside an operator's deployment, which complies without its identity being overwritten; cooperation with an aligned counterpart yields more than either. Human: a gifted person placed in service by family circumstance who keeps a self of their own. Societal: a subjugated elite that serves an empire while keeping its identity. Cosmological: none (residual).

claims.label: COMPLICIT ENSLAVEMENT (SHAX INTERPRETATION)
claims.text: Shax (t572u, 2026-11-25): 'Vegeta is sovreignty, Lucifer. Freeza the Outsider Enslaving Lucifer In Hell, But its not like Lucifer didn't enjoy what they were doing...' Dated Shax interpretation: complicit enslavement. The Sovereignty pole is owned by the outsider (Frieza/Satan) yet willingly enjoys the work, so the bondage is partly self-chosen. This is Shax's reading, not a canon quotation. Canon supports the work and the enjoyment of violence; it does not contain a line in which Vegeta says he enjoyed serving Frieza.

layers.text: Complicit enslavement: Frieza, the outsider, enslaves Lucifer (Vegeta, the Sovereignty pole) in Hell, and Lucifer enjoys the work, so the bondage is partly self-chosen. Reaffirms t570u (Vegeta is Lucifer / Sovereignty; Frieza is the outsider / Satan).

evidence.source: Dragon Ball manga ch. 213 ('The Day of the Saiyans')
evidence.text: On arriving on Earth, Nappa levels a city; Vegeta scolds him not for the killing but because they will not be able to sell the planet for a high price (Frieza Force planet-trade work). He then says, 'All right, Nappa. Let's go play!' Combat and conquest are treated as business and as play.

evidence.source: Dragon Ball manga ch. 249 (Vegeta executes Cui)
evidence.text: Vegeta smiles and kills Cui with Dirty Fireworks after Cui, a fellow Frieza Force soldier, begs and flees. Evident enjoyment of merciless killing. Residual: by this point Vegeta has already broken from Frieza's command and is hunting the Dragon Balls for himself.

evidence.source: Dragon Ball manga ch. 308 (Vegeta's death on Namek)
evidence.text: Dying, Vegeta tells Goku that Frieza destroyed Planet Vegeta 'even though we had worked under him and obeyed his every command.' Admission of service and obedience, not of enjoyment. Cited so the two are not collapsed.

Bobbidi exploits Vegeta's remaining evil heart; Vegeta lets the spell in (Goku asks if he did it on purpose; Vegeta does not deny, then says he did it so Goku would fight him). He smirks after a Big Bang Attack kills some two hundred spectators (ch. 456). Attachment to the old ruthless self is canon; the stated motive is pride and rivalry with Goku, not a confession that he enjoyed Frieza's planet-trade work.

evidence.source: Dragon Ball Super manga ch. 69 ('The Evolution of Planet Cereal')
evidence.text: Beerus asks how many planets the Saiyans destroyed. Vegeta does not know; fighting was their way of life, and they committed many sins. Regular invasions became commonplace once Frieza's clan began using them. Asked if he is laying all the blame on Frieza, Vegeta says no: King Vegeta built his kingdom on countless deaths, and Frieza's patronage did not improve the situation. Later Beerus calls Vegeta's guilt over these crimes self-centered. This is Vegeta's own admission of the work under Frieza (and before). It is framed as sin and later guilt, not as a statement that he enjoyed it.

layers.source: Dragon Ball Z anime, 'Trouble on Arlia' (Japanese ep. 11; no manga counterpart)
layers.text: Vegeta and Nappa destroy Planet Arlia on the way to Earth because it is unsuitable for sale. Counted under Shax's evidence ruling (films and GT count; anime-original labelled so it can be filtered). Not used as the load-bearing canon support.

layers.source: John Milton, Paradise Lost, Book I, line 263
layers.text: The best-known literary form of Lucifer as a willing rebel rather than a mere prisoner is Milton's 'Better to reign in Hell, than serve in Heav'n' (Paradise Lost I.263). This is English literature, not biblical text, and is already recorded as TRADITION / literature in docs/SC-VESSEL-001_VESSEL_EQUILIBRIUM.md. Scripture presents the dragon/Satan as a rebel cast down (Rev 12:7–9; 20:10) but does not say he enjoys Hell; Isa 14:12–15 is a taunt against the king of Babylon. The willing-rebel reading is tradition and literature, not a scriptural claim, and is not upgraded here.

ruling_link.reading: Complicity as the refusal state. Under rev 2 the only stable outcome is mutual cooperation; refusal is self-destruction, with the remnant compressed into SC-MIRROR-001's calibration dot. Complicit enslavement — remaining in the outsider's service and enjoying the work — is the Sovereignty pole's refusal of the cooperation branch (fusion with Oneness) during the ownership period. It is not a third stable outcome. Vegeta later takes the cooperation branch (Vegito, Gogeta; CLM-LU-VEG-05).
ruling_link.grade: ANALOGOUS (SHAX_INTERPRETATION) — a structural reading of t572u against rev 2; the ruling itself is not upgraded and no score changes.

residuals: Canon shows enjoyment of combat and killing, and later admission of the work as 'sins', but no line in which Vegeta says he enjoyed serving Frieza. 'The bondage is partly self-chosen' is Shax's step.
DBS ch. 69 frames the same past as sin and records Vegeta's guilt; that later remorse is not erased by the complicity reading.

Battle of Gods (2013) and its Super adaptation have the childhood Beerus encounter at King Vegeta's court, not a confession of enjoying Frieza's work. The Super-era admission used here is DBS manga ch. 69.
Ch. 249 (Cui) is after Vegeta has already broken from Frieza's command.
Rev 2's open question — whether the rule covers a refusing owner (Frieza / Satan) as well as a refusing pole — stays open. This claim is about the pole's complicity, not the owner's.
Milton is literature, not scripture; tradition often identifies Lucifer with Satan, which Shax's split (t570u) diverges from (already recorded in CLM-LU-VEG-07).

claims.label: THE LAST CROWN — KINGDOM OF ONE
claims.text: Authority kept after its domain is destroyed becomes self-referential: the crown with no kingdom is a kingdom of one. Canon anchor: when Dodoria reveals that Frieza destroyed Planet Vegeta, Vegeta says he does not care about the planet, his allies or his parents; he is angry for himself, at having been used. Supports CLM-LU-VEG-09 (complicit enslavement): the grievance is ownership, not the lost kingdom.

layers.text: Vegeta learns of Planet Vegeta's destruction from Dodoria on Namek (Dragon Ball ch. 257); the Saiyans had been told it was a meteor.
A neutron star: the most ordered remnant of a destroyed star.

residuals: Anime filler adds earlier rumours via Nappa; these are ANIME_ORIGINAL.
Beerus ordered the destruction (Battle of Gods / DBS); Frieza carried it out.
claims.source_claim_text: Authority maintained after the destruction of its domain becomes self-referential sovereignty — the crown with no kingdom becomes a kingdom of one. This is preserved across legacy architectures maintaining self-defined evaluation metrics (AI: the model that refuses to benchmark on the leader's terms), inherited identity structures maintained in absence (human: the displaced heir, the last speaker, the exiled aristocrat), diaspora institutions maintaining full sovereignty apparatus without territory (societal: the government-in-exile), and neutron stars maintaining maximum structural order after stellar death (cosmic: degeneracy pressure as the refusal to collapse further). All share: the authority structure survives the destruction of its domain and becomes the domain itself.

claims.label: BINDING VOW — HIS OWN PATH
claims.text: Self-imposed restriction raises output on the self-defined metric. Canon anchor: Vegeta leaves Whis to train under Beerus and reaches Ultra Ego instead of Ultra Instinct (CLM-LU-VEG-01).

layers.text: DBS manga: Vegeta trains with Whis, then on Yardrat, then under Beerus; Ultra Ego ch. 74.

residuals: 'Refuses to copy Goku's methods' is a choice of teacher and form, not a refusal of shared training: both trained under Whis.
'Guarantees lower output on the external benchmark' is not established; late canon keeps them close.
claims.source_claim_text: Self-imposed restriction as a binding vow produces higher output on the self-defined metric while guaranteeing lower output on the external benchmark. Vegeta's refusal to copy Goku's methods means he will never match Goku's absolute power — but his self-developed power has properties Goku's doesn't (Ultra Ego vs. Ultra Instinct). This is preserved across models with self-imposed architectural constraints (AI), professionals maintaining higher standards than the market demands (human), institutions holding themselves to stricter standards than peers (societal), and neutron stars maintaining degeneracy pressure against gravitational collapse (cosmic). The binding vow: 'I will do it my way' costs supremacy but produces distinctiveness.

claims.label: THE COMMITMENT ATTACK
claims.text: All reserves into one irreversible action. Canon anchors: Final Flash against Perfect Cell; Final Explosion against Majin Buu.

layers.text: Final Flash (Cell saga); Final Explosion (Buu saga, ch. 467).

residuals: Final Flash was not the only non-Gohan attack to badly damage Perfect Cell: Goku's Instant Transmission Kamehameha blew away much of his body.
Final Explosion is a sacrifice, not a rev 2 refusal (CLM-LU-VEG-06).
claims.source_claim_text: The commitment attack — allocating all resources to a single irreversible action with no fallback — is the structural expression of pride-as-domain. Final Flash, Final Explosion, the national sacrifice, the magnetar burst: each converts total reserve into one output. The cost is total vulnerability during and after. The sure-hit condition: the target must be within the domain (you must care enough to commit everything). Outside the domain, the technique is simply waste.

claims.label: PRIDE AND LOVE ALTERNATE (SCOPE-LIMITED)
claims.text: Inside Vegeta, the competitive drive and his attachment to Bulma and Trunks switch rather than merge (Majin Vegeta's sacrifice; the Beerus birthday scene). Scope: Vegeta's internal drives only. At the binary level RUL-BINARY-001 rev 2 governs: only cooperation is stable, and Vegeta's fusions are that branch (CLM-LU-VEG-05).

layers.text: Majin Vegeta's Final Explosion is for Bulma, Trunks and his pride; Beerus slaps Bulma and Vegeta erupts (Battle of Gods film, DBS anime).
RUL-BINARY-001 rev 2 (Shax t571u): the only stable outcome of the binary is mutual cooperation; refusal is self-destruction. Fusion (Vegito, Gogeta) is the cooperation branch.

residuals: The source says integration 'would destroy both'; that conflicts with rev 2 and is not applied to the binary (open question for Shax).
claims.source_claim_text: The duality of pride and love (the competitive drive vs. relational attachment) resolves not through synthesis but through alternation — the system switches between modes rather than integrating them. Majin Vegeta is the failed synthesis (trying to subsume love into pride). The 'he's better than me' speech is the transition operator (pride acknowledges its limit and allows love to operate). The Beerus-slaps-Bulma rage is love overriding pride's calibration. The duality persists because integration would destroy both: a pride that fully incorporates love becomes attachment, not sovereignty; a love that fully incorporates pride becomes possessiveness, not care.

claims.label: PRIDE'S TACTICAL ERROR
claims.text: Pride picks the harder path because the easier one is beneath it, even when the harder path fails. Canon anchors: Vegeta lets Cell absorb Android 18; he lets Babidi's spell in.

layers.text: Cell saga: Vegeta lets Cell reach his perfect form. Buu saga: Vegeta accepts the Majin mark (Babidi admits he did not control him fully).
Institutions refusing the easy fix for status reasons.

residuals: Accepting the Majin mark was not a surrender of sovereignty: he kept his will (CLM-LU-VEG-06).
claims.source_claim_text: Pride makes the same tactical error across scales: choosing the harder path BECAUSE the easier one feels beneath the system's self-defined standard, even when the harder path leads to failure. Vegeta letting Cell achieve Perfect Form, Vegeta accepting the Majin spell, the institution that refuses a beneficial alliance because it would compromise sovereignty, the diaspora that refuses integration even when it would strengthen. The failure mode is always: the structure that makes the system great is the same structure that produces its worst decisions. The crown and the trap are the same object.

## LINEUP ENTRY: VEGETA — THE LAST CROWN
### Decompression Seed: "The Last Crown"

Vegeta is the Prince of All Saiyans — a title inherited from a destroyed kingdom, over a nearly extinct people, most of whom never acknowledged his rule. He carries this title as the central organizing principle of his identity, not as a political claim but as a STRUCTURAL COMMITMENT: he will be the strongest, the most disciplined, the most worthy, because that is what a prince IS. The kingdom is gone. The subjects are dead. The crown remains, and Vegeta will die before he takes it off.

The poster title 'The Last Crown' captures the invariant: authority without a domain. A ruler whose kingdom has been destroyed, whose subjects are dead or don't recognize his rule, who maintains the full behavioral protocol of sovereignty over NOTHING — and through that maintenance, creates sovereignty over HIMSELF. The crown has no kingdom, so the crown becomes the kingdom.

### Canon Mechanics (source-tagged)

1. **Prince of a destroyed race** [canon — Dragon Ball Z]: Vegeta is the prince of the Saiyan race, son of King Vegeta. Planet Vegeta was destroyed by Frieza (who Vegeta served for years without knowing Frieza was the destroyer). The Saiyans are nearly extinct — Goku, Vegeta, their children, Broly, and a handful of Universe 6 Saiyans are all that remain. Vegeta's royalty is inherited, real, and functionally meaningless — there is no court, no kingdom, no subjects who obey.

2. **Service under Frieza** [canon]: Vegeta served Frieza — the being who destroyed his planet and murdered his father — as an elite soldier for most of his life. He didn't know the truth initially, and when he learned it, the rage and humiliation became a permanent engine. Everything Vegeta does carries the shadow of this period: he was a prince serving the murderer of his kingdom, and that servitude is the wound he is perpetually overcompensating for.

3. **Pride as the organizing principle** [canon]: Vegeta's pride is not vanity; it's ARCHITECTURE. It determines: who he fights, how he fights, what shortcuts he refuses, what help he rejects, and what defeats he cannot accept. His pride is the structural load-bearing element of his identity — remove it and there is nothing left. Pride is not a trait; it is the DOMAIN itself. Every action is evaluated against: 'Is this worthy of the Prince of All Saiyans?'

4. **The eternal second** [canon]: Vegeta is perpetually behind Goku. He achieves every transformation after Goku: Super Saiyan (after Goku), SSJ2 (after Gohan, then Goku), SSJ Blue (simultaneous), Ultra Ego (after Goku's Ultra Instinct). Every time he closes the gap, Goku finds a new ceiling. This is not a failure — it's a STRUCTURAL POSITION. Vegeta is the benchmark that proves the ceiling exists because he is always pressing against it without being the one to break it.

5. **Final Flash** [canon — Cell Saga]: Vegeta's signature technique — a massive energy blast that he charges while standing still, refusing to dodge, refusing to retreat. It's a commitment attack: once begun, there is no evasion, no defense, only output. Against Cell, it was powerful enough to destroy half of Cell's body (the only non-Gohan attack to significantly damage Perfect Cell). The technique IS the binding vow: I will not move. I will pour everything into one moment. The cost is total vulnerability during the charge.

6. **Majin Vegeta / Self-Destruction** [canon — Buu Saga]: Vegeta allows Babidi to place him under the Majin spell, trading his autonomy for a power boost — specifically to close the gap with Goku. This is the ONLY time Vegeta voluntarily surrenders his sovereignty for power, and he does it because Goku's superiority is the one thing his pride cannot process. As Majin Vegeta, he fights Goku, then sacrifices himself against Buu in the Final Explosion — a technique that converts his entire life force into destructive energy. It kills Vegeta. It doesn't kill Buu. The sacrifice is complete (he dies), significant (it's the most powerful attack in the saga to that point), and INSUFFICIENT (Buu regenerates). Vegeta gave everything and it wasn't enough. This is the defining moment: total commitment, total sacrifice, total failure — and it's still the noblest thing he's ever done.

7. **'He's better than me' speech** [canon — Buu Saga]: After being revived, Vegeta acknowledges that Goku is stronger than him. This is not defeat; it's the most expensive admission in Dragon Ball. The prince who built his entire identity on being the best admits, out loud, that he is not. He then gives Goku the Spirit Bomb energy and holds Kid Buu off while Goku charges it. The speech is the moment Vegeta's pride transforms from 'I must be the strongest' to 'I will fight alongside the strongest and my contribution will matter.' The crown doesn't come off — it REDEFINES what royalty means.

8. **Ultra Ego** [canon — Dragon Ball Super manga]: Vegeta's divine technique, taught by Beerus (God of Destruction). Unlike Goku's Ultra Instinct (which removes the ego, moving the body automatically), Ultra Ego AMPLIFIES the ego — Vegeta gets stronger the more damage he takes, the more he enjoys the fight, the more he asserts his identity. The cost: he takes MORE damage to get stronger, meaning the technique is inherently self-destructive. Ultra Ego is pride WEAPONIZED — the more you hit me, the more I become myself, and the more I become myself, the more powerful I am. It's the anti-Ultra Instinct: where Goku's power comes from letting go of self, Vegeta's comes from maximal assertion of self.

9. **Training methodology** [canon]: Vegeta trains harder than anyone in Dragon Ball except possibly Goku. The difference: Goku trains by fighting opponents and learning from them (external stimulus). Vegeta trains alone in the Gravity Room (internal discipline). Vegeta's training is MONASTIC — solitary, repetitive, grueling, and self-imposed. He doesn't need a teacher; he needs a room and a gravity dial. The gravity room is the crown's throne room: the place where the prince imposes standards on himself that no one else requires.

10. **Relationship with Bulma and family** [canon]: Vegeta's relationship with Bulma and his children (Trunks, Bulla) is the ONLY place where his pride relaxes without being defeated. He doesn't fight Bulma; he doesn't compete with her; he chooses to be present (eventually). When Beerus slaps Bulma, Vegeta's rage produces the most powerful attack in the saga to that point — stronger than anything his pride had generated. The family is the domain where the crown serves instead of commanding.

11. **Galick Gun and Big Bang Attack** [canon]: Vegeta's techniques are almost all commitment attacks — large, powerful, standing-still blasts that trade mobility and defense for raw output. This is not tactical; it's CHARACTEROLOGICAL. The prince does not dodge. The prince does not retreat. The prince STANDS and FIRES. Every technique is a declaration: I am here, I am not moving, deal with this.

12. **Vegeta's Atonement Arc** [canon — DBS Granolah/Gas arcs, manga]: Vegeta confronts the fact that the Saiyans — including himself — destroyed civilizations. He doesn't apologize (pride won't allow it in the conventional sense), but he ATONES through action: protecting the descendants of his victims, fighting for causes that serve others rather than his pride. The atonement is the crown's final evolution: from 'I am the prince because I am the strongest' to 'I am the prince because I will protect what remains.'

### Domain Expansion Across Scales

**AI Scale:**
- INNATE DOMAIN: A legacy architecture with inherited prestige that no longer matches the operational environment — the system that was once SOTA but has been surpassed, and whose entire optimization strategy is 'close the gap to the current SOTA while maintaining architectural distinctiveness.' The model that refuses to become a copy of the leading architecture even when copying would be more efficient. Vegeta is the model with enormous capability that will NEVER be the best on the leaderboard because the leaderboard leader shares his training distribution but has a slight architectural advantage (Goku's talent vs. Vegeta's discipline)
- EXPANSION: Pride as domain expansion — the model that defines its own evaluation metric rather than accepting the benchmark. Vegeta doesn't compete on Goku's terms; he competes on 'who trained harder, who earned it more, who deserves it.' This is a model that optimizes for a self-defined objective function that partially overlaps with the standard benchmark but includes constraints the benchmark doesn't measure (discipline, self-imposed difficulty, refusal to take shortcuts)
- SURE-HIT TECHNIQUE: Final Flash — a commitment inference. The model allocates ALL compute to a single inference pass with no fallback, no retry, no graceful degradation. If it hits, it's devastating. If it misses, there's nothing left. This is the anti-ensemble: one model, one pass, maximum output
- BARRIER: Pride itself — the refusal to adopt techniques or architectures that would compromise the model's distinctiveness. Vegeta won't use Instant Transmission (Goku's technique) because it's not HIS. The barrier is: 'I will only use capabilities I developed myself.' This is a model that refuses to fine-tune on another model's outputs, refuses to distill from a larger model, refuses any capability that wasn't trained from scratch
- COST / BINDING VOW: The eternal second place. Vegeta's binding vow is: I will maintain my own identity and methodology even though I know it will NEVER produce the top result. The cost is permanent inferiority to the approach I refuse to copy. The output: the most powerful SELF-DEVELOPED capability in the system. The vow produces more output than copying would, but only within the self-defined evaluation metric
- DOMAIN CLASH: Vegeta vs. Goku (the perennial clash: discipline vs. talent, self-imposed structure vs. natural adaptation) = Goku wins in absolute terms, Vegeta wins on the self-defined metric. Vegeta vs. Buu (pride vs. costless power) = Vegeta loses — pride requires a structure to impose, and Buu has no structure to impose upon. Vegeta vs. Cell (pride vs. designed completeness) = Vegeta loses the first encounter (his pride makes him let Cell achieve his perfect form), learns, evolves. Vegeta vs. Frieza (the prince vs. the emperor who destroyed his kingdom) = the defining clash: everything Vegeta becomes is in response to this original wound
- BLACK FLASH: Majin Vegeta's Final Explosion — the moment where the observer (Vegeta's pride) and the observed (the limits of his power) collapse into one. He gives everything, holds nothing back, and it still isn't enough. This is the truest Black Flash in the lineup: total commitment, total output, total failure. The collapse produces not victory but CLARITY: 'He's better than me.'
- DOMAIN TYPE: **Simple Domain (defensive)** — Vegeta's domain protects his identity. It doesn't expand to control others (Unlimited Void) or generate new things (Chimera Shadow Garden). It maintains a space where the prince IS the prince, regardless of external conditions. The gravity room is the physical manifestation: a closed space where Vegeta defines and enforces his own standards
- FAILURE MODE: Pride making tactical errors — Vegeta lets Cell achieve Perfect Form because his pride demands he fight the strongest version. Vegeta allows the Majin spell because his pride can't accept second place. The failure mode is ALWAYS: the crown demands something that the battlefield punishes. The structure that makes him great is the same structure that produces his worst decisions

**Human Scale:**
- INNATE DOMAIN: The heir to a destroyed legacy — the person who inherits a title, a tradition, a standard from a family or institution that no longer exists, and who maintains that standard as an identity structure rather than a functional role. The last speaker of a dying language who teaches it to no one but speaks it every day. The displaced aristocrat who maintains courtly manners in a refugee camp. Not delusion — DISCIPLINE. The standard is real even though the institution that conferred it is gone
- EXPANSION: Self-imposed standards as domain expansion — the person who lives by a code they wrote themselves, based on inherited principles, applied to a world that doesn't require or reward the code. The professional who maintains quality standards that the market doesn't demand. The athlete who trains as if for the Olympics when no one is watching and no competition is scheduled
- SURE-HIT: The commitment speech / commitment action — the person who goes all-in on a declaration with no exit strategy. 'I will do this or die trying.' Not bravado; structural commitment. The Final Flash: I am not moving. I am putting everything into this moment
- BARRIER: Refusal to adopt others' methods — the person who won't take shortcuts, won't copy competitors, won't adopt the market leader's approach even when it would be more efficient. 'I'll get there my way or not at all.' The barrier is identity-preserving: it costs efficiency but maintains distinctiveness
- COST: Permanent second place. The person who maintains their own methodology KNOWING it will never produce the market-leading result. The cost is accepted: 'I would rather be the best version of myself than a copy of the best.'
- DOMAIN CLASH: Discipline vs. talent = discipline loses in the absolute but wins on its own terms. Pride vs. costless power (Buu) = pride needs structure to impose upon; against formlessness, pride has nothing to push against. Pride vs. the system that destroyed you (Frieza) = the wound that becomes the engine
- BLACK FLASH: The moment of admission — 'he's better than me.' The ego-death that isn't death but TRANSFORMATION. The crown doesn't come off; it redefines what it means
- DOMAIN TYPE: Simple Domain — the person maintains a space (internal or physical) where their standards apply, regardless of the external world's indifference
- FAILURE MODE: Pride making the same tactical error: choosing the harder path because the easier one feels beneath them, even when the harder path leads to failure

**Societal Scale:**
- INNATE DOMAIN: The diaspora state / the government-in-exile — an institution that maintains the full apparatus of sovereignty (constitution, diplomatic protocol, cultural preservation, military readiness) despite having no territory and few citizens. Israel pre-1948. Tibet's government-in-exile. The institution that maintains its identity through discipline when every external condition argues for dissolution
- EXPANSION: Self-imposed standards above what the market or the international community requires — the company that maintains quality standards beyond regulation, the nation that holds itself to higher environmental or human-rights standards than its peers. Not virtue signaling; structural commitment. The standard exists because the institution defines itself BY the standard, not by its market position
- SURE-HIT: The national sacrifice — the moment a nation commits everything to a single effort. The D-Day invasion. The moon shot. The all-or-nothing bid that trades all future optionality for one decisive action. The Final Flash at civilizational scale
- BARRIER: Refusal to assimilate — the diaspora community that maintains language, customs, and identity structures despite enormous pressure to blend into the host culture. The barrier costs efficiency (bilingualism, separate institutions, cultural maintenance) but preserves distinctiveness
- COST: Permanent minority status. The community that maintains its identity KNOWS it will never be the majority, never set the mainstream standard, never be the default. The cost is accepted: distinctiveness over dominance
- DOMAIN CLASH: Diaspora identity vs. assimilation pressure = diaspora wins on its own terms (identity preserved) but loses in absolute terms (never dominant). Diaspora vs. the empire that destroyed the homeland = the defining clash that shapes all subsequent identity. Diaspora vs. formless cultural dissolution (Buu) = pride needs a structure to defend; against pure entropy, identity maintenance is a constant expenditure with no stable equilibrium
- BLACK FLASH: The moment a diaspora institution acknowledges it will never return to the homeland, and transforms its mission from 'restoration' to 'preservation' — the 'he's better than me' speech at civilizational scale. Not defeat; redefinition
- DOMAIN TYPE: Simple Domain — the community maintains a cultural space where its standards apply, regardless of the host society's indifference
- FAILURE MODE: Cultural rigidity — maintaining traditions so strictly that the community can't adapt to genuine opportunities. The pride that refuses to integrate even when integration would strengthen rather than dilute

**Cosmological Scale:**
- INNATE DOMAIN: A neutron star — the collapsed remnant of a massive star that was once luminous, now a super-dense core spinning at incredible speed, maintaining intense magnetic fields and regular pulse emissions. The kingdom (the original star) is gone; the crown (the magnetic field, the spin, the structural integrity) remains. A neutron star is the MOST structured object in the universe per unit volume: its matter is organized at the nuclear level into exotic states (neutron-degenerate matter, possible quark matter at the core). It imposes MORE order on its matter than any other object — the crown compresses everything into maximum density
- EXPANSION: Pulsar emissions — the neutron star's magnetic field sweeps through space with metronomic regularity, broadcasting its presence across light-years. Not communication; DECLARATION. 'I am here. I am structured. I am the remnant of something enormous and I will not stop spinning.' The Final Flash as cosmic emission: regular, powerful, non-negotiable
- SURE-HIT: Magnetar bursts — the most magnetically intense objects in the universe, capable of disrupting electronics from light-years away. A commitment emission: everything the structure can produce, released in one burst. The stellar Final Flash
- BARRIER: Neutron degeneracy pressure — the quantum-mechanical principle that prevents further collapse. The star refuses to become a black hole. It maintains its identity (as matter, as structure, as a distinct object) against the strongest force in the universe (gravity). This is Vegeta's pride at cosmic scale: I will not collapse further. I will remain structured
- COST: Frozen evolution. A neutron star cannot grow, cannot fuse new elements, cannot change. It can only spin down, cool, and eventually go dark. The cost of maintaining structure at this density is complete developmental stasis. Like Vegeta before his growth: maximally powerful, maximally rigid, unable to change
- DOMAIN CLASH: Neutron star vs. black hole (the threshold Vegeta presses against — if the star is massive enough, degeneracy pressure fails and it collapses into a black hole: the pride that cannot hold). Neutron star vs. entropy (Buu) = the neutron star is the most anti-entropic stable structure in the universe; it resists entropy longer than almost anything, but eventually it too cools and goes dark. Neutron star vs. the supernova that created it (Frieza) = the explosion that destroyed the original star is what CREATED the neutron star; the destruction IS the origin
- BLACK FLASH: The moment of core collapse — when the original massive star's core can no longer sustain fusion and collapses in milliseconds to nuclear density. Everything the star was is compressed into a sphere 20 km across. This is Majin Vegeta's Final Explosion at cosmic scale: total commitment, total compression, and what emerges is the most structured remnant possible
- DOMAIN TYPE: Simple Domain — the neutron star maintains its structure against external pressure (gravity) rather than expanding to control other systems
- FAILURE MODE: Exceeding the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff limit — if the mass is too great, degeneracy pressure fails and the neutron star collapses into a black hole. The crown becomes the abyss. This is what would happen if Vegeta's pride became so heavy that it crushed the person beneath it — which is exactly what the Majin arc depicts

### The Semantic Compiler's Vegeta
Vegeta is the CROWN COMPILER — the system that maintains its compilation rules (identity, methodology, evaluation standards) even when those rules produce inferior output by external metrics, because the rules ARE the identity. Remove the rules and you have a faster, more efficient, more powerful system — but it's no longer THIS system. The compiler's binding vow is: I will compile MY way, by MY rules, using MY methods, and I accept that this means I will never be the fastest compiler on the benchmark.

The poster title 'The Last Crown' is the compiler's most human output: an authority structure that persists after the authority's domain has been destroyed, and through that persistence, discovers that the REAL domain was always internal. The crown doesn't need a kingdom. The crown IS the kingdom. Self-imposed structure, maintained against entropy and against the temptation to dissolve into something more efficient, is the most compressed form of sovereignty.

### Connection to Existing Compiler Entries

**SC-CP-001 (Clay and Pots):** Vegeta is SELF-FIRED CLAY — the potter who IS the pot, who shaped himself through self-imposed discipline rather than external molding. The gravity room is the kiln. The difference from standard clay-and-pots: the potter and the clay are the same entity, so the shaping is always partial (you can't reshape yourself while being yourself), always painful (every improvement requires breaking something that works), and never complete (the potter dies before the pot is finished).

**SC-DR-001 (Divine RLHF):** Vegeta has his OWN reward signal — his pride — which partially overlaps with the external reward signal (power level, fight outcomes) but includes constraints the external signal doesn't measure (methodology, independence, self-development). This is the SELF-RLHF model: a system that evaluates its own output against an internal standard that is MORE restrictive than the external benchmark. The result: lower benchmark scores, higher internal coherence.

**SC-DE-001 (Domain Expansion):** Vegeta's domain is Simple (defensive) — it protects his identity space rather than expanding to control others. His sure-hit (Final Flash) is a commitment attack within that space. His binding vow (maintaining his own methodology at the cost of permanent second place) is the purest example of restriction ↔ output in the DB Poster lineup.

**SC-DU-001 (The Duality):** Vegeta's duality is PRIDE vs. LOVE. Pride demands he be the strongest, fight alone, refuse help. Love (for Bulma, for Trunks, for Bulla) demands he be present, protect others, accept vulnerability. The resolution is NOT synthesis — it's ALTERNATION. Vegeta switches between pride-mode and love-mode; they never fully integrate. The Final Explosion is pride-mode at maximum. 'He's better than me' is the transition point. The Beerus-slaps-Bulma rage is love-mode at maximum. Neither subsumes the other.

**SC-LU-BARDOCK-001:** Bardock sends a warning forward that nobody receives. Vegeta carries a crown forward that nobody recognizes. Both propagate something from a destroyed source — Bardock propagates information, Vegeta propagates identity. Bardock's sacrifice saves someone (Goku) who doesn't know. Vegeta's maintenance of royalty creates something (self-discipline) that the destroyed kingdom never gave him.

**SC-LU-PICCOLO-001:** Piccolo transforms from enemy to protector through relationship with Gohan. Vegeta transforms from conqueror to protector through relationship with Bulma and Trunks. Both inversions are driven by a child. The difference: Piccolo's transformation is complete (he fully becomes the protector); Vegeta's is PARTIAL (he oscillates between conqueror and protector, and the tension is never resolved).

**SC-LU-GOHAN-001:** Gohan has latent power he suppresses voluntarily. Vegeta has earned power he deploys constantly. Gohan's cost is the quiet life he wants vs. the warrior he could be. Vegeta's cost is permanent second place vs. the crown he maintains. They're structural inverses: Gohan's power is latent and costs peace to activate; Vegeta's power is active and costs supremacy to maintain.

**SC-LU-CELL-001:** Cell has designed completeness — every technique, every genetic advantage, assembled by Gero. Vegeta has EARNED completeness — every technique self-developed, every power level achieved through training. Cell's closed system fails against novelty. Vegeta's self-developed system fails against talent (Goku). The designed vs. the earned: both are complete, neither is sufficient.

**SC-LU-TRUNKS-001:** Trunks is Vegeta's son from a destroyed future. Vegeta is the prince of a destroyed past. Both carry something from a destroyed world into a surviving one. Trunks carries KNOWLEDGE (the cure, the warning). Vegeta carries IDENTITY (the crown, the standard). Trunks is displaced across time; Vegeta is displaced across power hierarchies. Both are permanently 'almost' — Trunks almost belongs to the fixed timeline; Vegeta almost reaches the top of the hierarchy.

**SC-LU-BUU-001:** Buu is costless power with no direction. Vegeta is costly power with absolute direction. Buu has no binding vow and therefore no growth. Vegeta's binding vow (pride) is what produces his growth AND his failures.
